topic: Building a crypto trading bot without knowing how to code
angle: Daan's own route: a trading bot built with Replit's AI agent and connected to the Bitvavo API. What it takes (writing rules, building with an AI assistant, testing small), honest about the cost of learning and the risks.

topic: What does it really cost to run your own trading bot?
angle: Honest cost items without inventing amounts: hosting, trading fees per transaction (lower at volume), AI assistant costs while building, and the cost of learning. A counterweight to 'free money' stories.

topic: The Bitvavo API explained for non-programmers
angle: What an exchange API is, why Daan chose Bitvavo (EU-regulated, euro), why trade-only API keys without withdrawal rights matter, and how his bot runs on it 24/7.

topic: AI automation for a one-person business
Build an AI agent yourself or have one built
A weekly routine for systematic trading
Trade-only API keys: the one setting that limits the damage
angle: Why Daan's bot uses an exchange API key that can place trades but cannot withdraw funds, what that protects against and what it does not (a bad strategy can still lose money). Where keys should live (environment secrets, never in code), and rotating them. Practical, no figures.

topic: How I keep an eye on a bot that trades while I sleep
angle: What monitoring a 24/7 bot involves in Daan's setup: a dashboard, Telegram alerts, a weekly report. The lesson that a report can be wrong while looking right: check its numbers against the exchange itself now and then. No returns, no figures.

topic: When an AI coding agent gets expensive: what I changed
angle: Daan built his bot with Replit's AI agent; because each change drew down agent credits, he moved code changes to Claude and kept the bot hosted on Replit. Explain effort-based billing in plain words, the trade-off, and when an agent is still the right tool. Neutral about Replit, no amounts.

topic: What an AI agent on a VPS actually does all day
angle: Victor, Daan's AI agent on a Hostinger VPS: scheduled jobs that build and check pages, a publishing chain with checks before anything goes live, and alerts when something fails. Honest that it needs supervision: an agent can repeat a mistake quietly until a check catches it. No invented incidents or durations.

topic: The checks I put between an AI agent and my live sites
angle: Why automated publishing needs gates: every change runs through checks (broken links, missing prices, claims without a source) before it goes live, and a failed check stops the run instead of publishing. What a one-person business can copy from that without writing much code. No figures.
